statement: It is an implied term in a contract for the supply of goods or services where the purchaser and supplier are each acting in the course of a business that a qualifying debt carries simple statutory interest, at 8 per cent per annum over the official dealing rate (Bank of England base rate) in force on the 30 June or 31 December immediately before the day statutory interest starts to run (Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998 s 1; Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Rate of Interest) (No. 3) Order 2002, SI 2002/1675, art 4).
caveat: Section 5A adds a fixed recovery sum once statutory interest runs (£40 for debts under £1,000, £70 from £1,000 to £9,999.99, £100 for £10,000 or more), plus reasonable recovery costs above the fixed sum. Consumer credit agreements and contracts operating as security are outside the Act, and contract terms can displace statutory interest only where they provide a substantial contractual remedy for late payment. This repo does not compute interest on a specific debt.
